text:
Maria L: quick proposal — trying a different slab-based cap for max-tokens-per-batch per cardclass to tame KV-fragmentation and p95 regressions. short TL;DR: allocate "slabs" (discrete max-token budgets) instead of one flat max, pick slab by sequence-length quantile and kernel-fit.

Kevin T: slab-based? can you sketch how we map slabs to GPUs (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100)?

Maria L: sketch below. goal: fewer cross-shape kernel fallbacks and less internal KV churn. slabs chosen so common seq_len buckets fill efficiently. example slab table I prototyped:

```
cardclass -> slabs (max_tokens_per_batch)
A100  -> [8192, 4096, 2048]
H100  -> [12288, 8192, 4096]
A10   -> [6144, 3072, 1536]
L4    -> [4096, 2048, 1024]
T4    -> [3072, 1536, 768]
```

Maria L: runtime will pick the slab by median prefix length in the current batch window and kernel selector will try kernels in descending slab order. If kernel-fit fails for slab, fallback to next slab (fast path).

Ashwin P: interesting. how does this interact with KV cache fragmentation? earlier runs showed mixed short+long killed p95 because of KV copies.

Maria L: good point — we add a small kv-coalesce step: when a long request would force copying many KV pages, route it to a larger slab that keeps it contiguous, otherwise prefer smaller slab that avoids creating new fragments. heuristics: if estimated kv-frag > 25% prefer next larger slab.

Jess R: do we have profiling to justify these slab numbers? I saw recent regressions after kernel selector change.

PerfBot: profile snapshot (recent canary run): p50 22ms, p95 310ms (+44ms baseline), tokens/sec -6%. top cause: KV memcpy spikes during mixed-shape batches. stacktrace points to kernel_fit fallback.

Maria L: right — bench runs: when mixing 512-token and 8192-token requests in same queue, kernel-selector kept picking big-kernels and falling back which cost ~30-60ms per request. slab limits reduce fallback frequency in synthetic mix tests by ~70%.

Kevin T: sounds promising. rollout plan? canary -> 10% -> 50%? any safety gates?

Maria L: proposed rollout:
- canary 5% per region for 24h, collect p50/p95, tail-error-rate, kernel-fallback-rate, GPU-util, tokens/sec
- if kernel-fallback-rate drops >= 40% and p95 doesn't regress > +10ms -> expand to 50%
- monitor KV-mem-alloc churn metric (kv_frag_bytes / total_kv_bytes) must not increase > 5%

Ashwin P: what about slot packing fairness? slabs could favor long requests and starve short ones.

Maria L: queue policy change: when slab chosen, enforce weight = tokens^(0.6) soft priority so short requests still get chances. also add token-budget per slot window: each slot has token_budget = slab * 1.2, refill every 100ms.

Jess R: can we see the config snippet we would apply (so infra can review)?

Maria L: config proto (canary):
```
batching: {
  slab_scheme: true,
  cardclass_slabs: {
    "A100": [12288,8192,4096],
    "H100": [16384,12288,8192],
    "A10": [6144,3072,1536],
    "L4": [4096,2048,1024],
    "T4": [3072,1536,768]
  },
  slab_selection: "median_seq_quantile",
  kv_coalesce_threshold: 0.25,
  slot_refill_ms: 100,
  slot_token_budget_factor: 1.2,
  slot_weight_exponent: 0.6
}
```

PerfBot: quick sim results from local runner (mixed 512/8192 load):
- baseline p95 342ms -> slab p95 280ms (18% improvement)
- kernel-fallback-rate 0.37 -> 0.11
- tokens/sec +3%
- KV-frag bytes delta +1.8% (within gate)

Kevin T: nice. does this change kernel selector ordering? might need to update our kernel tables for H100 microkernels.

Maria L: yes we'll push kernel-affinity hints: prefer kernel variant X for slabs >=8192 on H100/A100. small change in selector costs but reduces fallback.

Jess R: testing matrix? we should include sessions with heavy cache hits vs cold-starts.

Maria L: plan to run:
- synthetic mixes (512/2048/8192) across cardclasses
- replay 48h production traces in staging with slab enabled vs disabled
- controlled canary in us-west and eu-west

Ashwin P: might be tricky for Dedicated customers with pinned capacity. will this be opt-in?

Maria L: default-on for hosted runtime, opt-out flag for Dedicated/Private. we'll add runtime flag: `batching.slab_scheme.enabled=false` for dedicated profiles.

Kevin T: when do you want to cut the canary?

Maria L: aiming to enqueue the canary tomorrow 06:00 UTC after a short patch to kernel-hints. I'll create the PR and attach perf dashboards.

release-bot: deployment scheduled: patch/4301-batch-slab -> canary at 2026-03-19T06:00:00Z (dry-run flagged).

Jess R: add me as reviewer on the PR, I'll run the staging trace replay. also add a brief runbook for rollback (how to flip flag).

Maria L: will do, PR in ~1h. collecting owners: @Kevin T for kernel hints, @Ashwin P for slot policy sanity, @Jess R for validation. :rocket:

Kevin T: ack.

Ashwin P: ack.

Jess R: ack, will check dashboards post-canary.
